analysis:
Only BASE text for MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift was supplied, plus a truncated patch excerpt (patch_excerpt_complete=false). The head-side ranges (512-519, 985-1006, 1126, 1153, 1187, 1231-1241, 1300-1302, 1309, 1419, 1470, 1490-1493, 1590, 1597-1598) are mostly not visible, so I could not verify them.

Visible changes:
(1) A new fail-closed guard. GLM media requests that need withheld output (JSON response_format or required/named tool_choice) now fire releaseBox and throw invalidToolPayload. This runs before the media path (base ~509-520), so it avoids serving unvalidated forced-call or JSON output on the media path. It is a tightening, not a regression. releaseBox.fire() is called before the throw, so the model pin is not leaked.
(2) A new withholdsGLMOutput flag on the text path ORs into usesNativeTextChannels for nativeReasoningPrefix (base ~989-993). GLM reasoning is then routed through the typed native channel, not leaked into content, while its output is withheld. The effect on withholdReasoning and reasoning disclosure cannot be verified without the GLM5NextPromptPolicy and NativeToolStreamRouter sources.

Unchanged base paths checked. Media reservation and release run on every exit (base 592-610, 697, 768, 806). Pre-content deadline checks release the lease and cancel upstream (base 1122-1154). The forwarding task and native-lease cancellation behave as before. Cache scope still comes only from requestCacheScope, which the coordinator authors (T-041). The media path still sets cacheEnabled false for native MiMo and uses hybridPrefixIdentity only for owned Qwen4 or diffusion. I saw no change to prefix-cache scoping, encryption, attestation or authorization.

Open integration questions: the head-side edits near 1231-1241 and 1490-1493 (forwarding and handoff cancellation), and the 1126/1153 closeAndCancel and release ordering. They could affect lease or pin release (availability, T-010) and must be checked against the full head text. No finding is reported because the evidence does not establish one.
